account:
Today has appeared to be an ordinary working day, with no confirmed emergency or unusual scheme. During my market walk, townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the bridge and market. I heard a distant shout and checked with the baker: he said he was advertising fresh bread, had collected eight emeralds in sales, and had a well-stocked stall. He asked whether municipal gatherings would need bread; I told him none were confirmed and that any future order would require discussion of quantity and price. The bread movements therefore seem consistent with stocking and selling at market, not evidence of wrongdoing.

I have sought a bridge and road repair proposal before authorizing expenditure. My notes indicate that the builder may have missed the inspection request, so I cannot assume an inspection or quote is underway. An office meeting is scheduled for 16:30. No spending has been authorized.

The neighbour confirmed our usual three o'clock tea at the east-bank dockside cottage, road point (16, -60, 105). The secretary had been asked to clarify the venue; I subsequently obtained confirmation directly from the neighbour. Earlier I saw the secretary take the appointment book from its chest, consistent with managing my schedule.

I attended the market walk and noon break at home and have now returned to the town hall for the 13:00 accounts appointment. I am beside the treasury chest but have not yet inspected its contents. Some conversations were too distant to understand, so I cannot infer their subjects. My next commitments are tea at 15:00, the office at 16:30, and home at 19:00.
